newsitem.title: UK: UK says no change in rural advertising controls.
newsitem.headline: UK says no change in rural advertising controls.

text.p: There will be no relaxation of controls on rural advertising in Britain, Planning Minister Robert Jones said on Tuesday.
Special controls were introduced to Britain in 1948 to prevent poster panels from flooding roadsides in rural areas.

After consideration of an extensive public consultation exercise over the future of special controls, "the Secretary of State has decided that they will remain for the time being," Jones told Parliament.

Asked what measures Britain's Planning authorities would take in the future, Jones said they would be looking to see if there are sensible modifications that can be made "to provide the same protection of amenity with less bureaucracy."

Jones said the removal of the Areas of Special Control advertisements regime would not have created an "open season" on advertising in the countryside as local planning authorities had widespread control over advertising.
